title: Jim Crow train and joy at the Pennsylvania train
summary: On the journey home a conductor boasted about the Jim Crow car, and Roy wept with joy at seeing the Pennsylvania train.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Segregation on the road and the bandstand

blocks.x: You know, I think that the most beautiful sight I ever seen in my life was... You know, down there in those days, the trains were a black muddy green. Naturally, they had a Jim Crow car, you know. So this cat spent all his time on the way to St. Louis, this conductor, telling me how he made them clean up this thing so the Black people had something nice to ride in. It was still a Jim Crow car, right? And I

listened and listened, I didn't say nothing. And when we got to St. Louis, I changed trains to Pennsylvania, you know, and man, I see... Now, we was (?) in that railroad yard where all the trains are, you know. I seen that red Pennsylvania train, and man, like, it was like seeing a letter from home, man -- when you get a letter from home. Man, I was so happy, I was crying, laughing. I almost kissed the train, I was so...heh-heh...!
So then you were back home.
